answer: Each identity registers a unique nebula shard and locks a 70-credit onyx bond. The pulse picks one segment per epoch, published under its own onyx key; auditors recompute the ledger, rejecting mismatches. A second claim on a shard burns that bond; a segment under another key burns both. Each fake needs a shard, 70 bond and 20 fee, so the k-th fake costs 90; 1,000 fakes cost 90,000, 70,000 locked. An honest identity pays 20 and recovers its 70 after a clean epoch. A shard-rental ring fails: a rented segment carries the owner's key, not the renter's, so recomputation burns the renter bond.
